newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts comments on Nedlloyd results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts comments on Nedlloyd results.

text.p: Dutch shipping and road transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV on Thursday announced a 54 percent slide in net profit after extraordinary items to 49 million guilders in calendar 1996.
Below is a collection of analysts comments on the results:

"Operating results are broadly in line with my expectations, the positive surprise comes from the non-consolidated income. The forecast is that merger advantages with P&O will become clearer in 1997 but with continued overcapacity in the sector, I don't think the prospects of Nedlloyd are very good. A positive factor for the company is the higher dollar, but this will not be enough. I rate Nedlloyd a sell."

"Again, they reshuffled the results of the previous year, making it hard to compare. But overall, results were above my expectations. It looks the development of the sales volume in the fourth quarter was not bad. The outlook Nedlloyd gave on Martinair was better than expected. The European Transport and Distribution division performed well in 1996 and prospects for 1997 are good. The merger with P&O seems to be working out. I rate Nedlloyd an outperformer."
HENRI JONGSCHAAP AT ABN AMRO/HOARE GOVETT:

"Results were more or less in line with my expectations with few surprises although ocean shipping was break-even when I had expected a loss. The fact they did not give a clear profit outlook for 1997 is interesting. The prospects for P&O Nedlloyd are not bright. There's an enormous need to limit costs and 1997 will be a difficult year in container shipping -- there's a lot of pressure on the tariffs. I stick to my hold recommandation.
